> I'm a PhD student in Tel Aviv University. I am working with the package,
> ggplot2, to generate my plots. Let me first say that it is an amazing
> package, much better for plot generating than any other package I was
> working with in R. However, I stumbled upon a possible bug (which might be
> in Rstudio rather than ggplot). When I'm adding a theme to the plot for
> changing the background of the plot to white or even just putting borders
> for the plot area it also adds borders to the whole plot. This makes a big
> problem when trying to put a few plots on one sheet. It creates borders
> between the four plots on the sheet.
>
> I tried every possible way I could think of to try and fix this. I tried
> googleing the problem but it doesn't seem to happen to anyone or people just
> don't blog about it.
>
> Do anyone know of this kind of problem and perhaps know's how I can fix
> this?

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Possible bug in ggplot2
parts:
Much easier. 

It's putting a black line around each panel because you've told it to. 

theme(plot.background = element_rect(colour="black"))

Either leave this line out or:

theme(plot.background = element_rect(colour=NA))

... and the lines go away. 

Is that what you want? I'm not entirely sure I understand the problem.

B
